intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Carroll County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated August 28, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Alpena
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor The governing body did not review the prior year report and accompanying comments at the first regularly scheduled meeting following receipt of the report, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-418.

cities.name: Beaver
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder Treasurer The Town paid $6,945 and $9,293 to the Mayor for park attendant services in 2024 and 2023, respectively. Town Council minutes indicate Ordinance no. 1001 was adopted to authorize these payments; however, a signed and complete copy of the ordinance was not provided for audit inspection.

cities.name: Blue Eye
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor The annual financial statements were not published or posted, as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 14-59-116.

cities.name: Eureka Springs
cities.quote: The result of our tests disclosed instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards and which are described in the Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting section as item 2024-1. We identified certain deficiencies in internal control, described below as item 2024-1, that we consider to be a material weakness.
